summary: Two persistent Wan-Animate-2 workers on four physical A800 GPUs generated all ten windows of the matched 660-frame source in 509.7154 seconds, 4.1096x faster than the historical per-window-reload baseline.
evidence: The matched baseline generated at 0.315074 useful FPS in 2094.7445 seconds and used 1.163747 A800 GPU-hours; the optimized run generated at 1.294840 useful FPS in 509.7154 seconds and used 0.566349 A800 GPU-hours.
End-to-end wall time decreased from 2153.1051 to 575.9873 seconds, a 3.7381x speedup, while measured A800 GPU-hours decreased 51.334%.
All 660 source frames are covered at 24 FPS; both workers loaded the model once and each completed a contiguous five-window temporal chain.
The benchmark report verifies identical source, identity reference, prompt, upstream/model revisions, checkpoint hashes, resolution, steps, guidance, and seed.
lessons: Persistent model residency removes nine repeated 14B checkpoint loads, and disjoint temporal-chain parallelism converts extra GPUs into useful wall-time speedup without increasing total GPU-hours.
limitations: The two independent temporal chains create one cross-batch boundary whose best-seam MAD is 14.2593, versus 3.5716-5.1175 for the rolling-reference overlaps.
The stitched radius-4 candidate remains review_required; its maximum transition ratio is 5.4317 and motion preservation is only 0.2938.
This establishes infrastructure throughput, not accepted contact physics, exact manipulation motion, or real-robot execution.
next_actions: Measure the complete source as one rolling temporal chain to quantify the continuity-first speed/quality tradeoff for videos longer than 20 seconds.
